curriculum: The Dutch-taught bachelor is 180 EC: 75 compulsory major credits, 30 further major-elective credits, 30 final research credits and 45 profiling credits. At least 22.5 EC of the 30 major-elective credits must be ISW electives. The programme permits flexible choices. To illustrate the first thematic group, choose Health in Society (level 2, Block 1 B), Challenges in Work, Health and Well-being (level 3, Block 2 C), Key Challenges to the Welfare State (level 2, Block 3 C) and Solidarity and Social Justice (level 3, Block 4 A). Sexuality and Society shares the Block 2 C slot with Work, Health and Well-being. The chosen group is spread across the four blocks and satisfies 15 EC at level 3 plus 15 EC at intermediate or higher level. Profiling remains open with at least 15 EC at level 2 or 3.
progression: Year 1 has the eight published compulsory courses, 60 EC. Year 2 can pair Health in Society (B) with Across Disciplinary Boundaries (A) in Block 1, and Work, Health and Well-being (C) with advanced research methods (AD) in Block 2. Welfare State and Solidarity and Social Justice fit in Blocks 3 and 4 respectively alongside eligible profiling electives. Year 3 can complete the remaining profiling in its first semester. The 7.5 EC literature study and 7.5 EC qualitative and quantitative analysis course occupy different timeslots (C and A) in Block 3, followed by the full 15 EC supervised project in Block 4. Literature and analysis prepare the same research sequence, and thesis research undergoes ethics review. The programme guide also offers the sequence in the first semester for eligible students. No numeric project-entry threshold is inferred from the unavailable regulations PDF.
